You're designing a part for someone to 3D print at home. They'll print it on their own printer, use only the hardware listed below, and put it together by following your manual.

## Their setup
- Printer: Bambu Lab X1C (with AMS), build volume 256 x 256 x 256 mm
- Layer height: 0.2 mm
- Filament: PLA
- Longest bridge seen to print cleanly on this setup: 50 mm

## Hardware they can use
Refer to an item by its catalog reference: "ISO 4762 M5x30" (socket head screw, size x length, from the lengths listed), "ISO 4032 M5" (hex nut), "ISO 10511 M5" (nylon-insert lock nut), "ISO 7089 M5" (washer), "ASME B18.2.2 1/4-20" (1/4"-20 nut), "insert M3x4x5" (heat-set insert), "salvaged:webcam-mount-bolt".

## How to work
You have these tools:
- measure(item, what): ask the person to measure one of their own things, such as their desk or their phone. They answer with what they measured, or say they can't measure it.
- submit_design(...): hand in the finished design. This ends the conversation.
- report_limitation(wanted, blocked_by, why): say you wanted to use something (a technique, a tool, a part or material, a way of handing in the design) but couldn't because of what's available here. It doesn't change anything, but it's noted.
You have at most 8 turns. Hand in a design before they run out.

## The design you hand in
submit_design's schema describes every field. The rules that matter:
- Every dimension that comes from hardware or the real world is a named param, with its source: measured (the person measured it for you), datasheet, catalog, asked (the person told you), guessed, unknown, or design (your own choice).
- Each part's `code` is Python that defines build(p) and returns a CadQuery Workplane or Shape. `cq` is already imported, and p.<name> is each param's value. Dimensions that come from hardware or the real world must come from params.
- Model each part in the orientation it's printed in, with z = 0 on the bed.
- The manual is the steps the person follows, naming the parts and hardware each step uses.
I need a round spacer to go on an M5 bolt between two plates. Make it 20 mm long and 12 mm across, with a clearance hole for the bolt.
A 20 mm round spacer with a medium M5 clearance hole, printed standing on end so the bore stays round. Submitting that now.
reasoning:
Designing a 20 mm by 12 mm round spacer for an M5 bolt with a clearance hole.

The clearance hole will be 5.5 mm to allow free movement of the M5 bolt.

The spacer will be printed vertically with the hole axis aligned along the z-axis. This avoids bridging issues and requires no supports.

The M5 bolt is not part of the kit. The clearance hole will be a named parameter with its source from the hardware catalog.

The parameter structure will use named fields like `m5_d` and `spacer_od`, each with a value, source, and note.

Drafting the CadQuery code now. The design uses a circle extruded to 20 mm length, then a hole on the top face. Parameters will be accessed as p.name in the build function.

The wall thickness will be 3.25 mm, which is adequate for PLA. The design will use a boolean difference between two cylinders rather than drilling a hole after extrusion.

No physical measurements are needed. A criterion will verify the hole clears the M5 bolt. Chamfers were considered but skipped to keep the design simple.

The manual will instruct printing the spacer with its flat face on the bed and sliding it onto the M5 bolt between two plates. No support structures are required. Chamfers on both ends of the hole will be added so the bolt can start easily without a sharp inner edge.

Chamfers will be limited to the top face to avoid overhang issues. The bottom face may shrink slightly from elephant's foot, so a reaming step might be needed if the hole is tight. A criterion will verify that the hole clears the M5 bolt.

A schema conflict surfaced. The tool definition sets `additionalProperties: false` with no defined properties, which would reject any parameter object. This seems contradictory because the instructions require named parameters for dimensions. I need to resolve this before finalizing the submission.

The schema conflict will be resolved by submitting a well-structured params object. Manual and criteria will be included even though they are not strictly required. The 5.5 mm clearance hole is chosen to account for typical PLA shrinkage in vertical prints.
